implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.3 (P06) apply to DSF-MES. Procedures PRC-02.1 to PRC-02.4 cover provisioning, certification, privileged access, and emergency access.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Repository, build, signing, and MES accounts are provisioned by identity governance from HR events and role templates approved by the system owner. Contractor accounts on the source repository are federated but depend on sponsor end dates. Gap: 9 of 60 sampled contractor departures kept repository access 4 to 21 days (POAM-002). MN-1 MES accounts are on a legacy directory with shared operator logins (POAM-007).
evidence: Identity governance role templates; repository user export; P07 AC-2 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Joiner, mover, and leaver events flow from the HR system to identity governance, which provisions and removes repository, build, signing portal, and FL-1 and TX-1 MES roles through connectors.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Workforce accounts inactive 45 days are disabled automatically, including federated repository accounts.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Account creation, modification, disabling, and removal are logged by identity governance and forwarded to the SIEM.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Repository branch protection enforces role-based write access; only release engineering can promote artifacts to the release repository; MES roles restrict recipe and firmware image selection to supervisors.
evidence: Branch protection export; artifact repository permissions; MES role matrix

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The build network zone accepts inbound connections only from the source repository service and the engineering zone; the signing service accepts requests only from the build orchestrator; plant programming stations pull released images from a plant image cache that is updated one way from the artifact repository.
evidence: Firewall rule sets; data flow diagram (P02 section 7)

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Separation of duties: developers cannot approve their own merge requests; release engineers cannot approve a signing request they submitted; the signing portal enforces two approvers from the product line's signing group. Gap: the legacy IV-300 1.x signing workstation relies on email approval with no enforced two-person control (POAM-001).
evidence: Signing portal approval configuration; P07 AC-5 results

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Least privilege through role templates and PAM for build servers, HSM administration, and MES servers. Gap: CI runners hold long-lived credentials with write access to the artifact repository (POAM-003).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Security functions (HSM administration, signing key ceremonies, PAM administration) are authorized to named roles only.
evidence: PAM role list; key ceremony records

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts, checked out through PAM, for non-security work only through their standard accounts.
Privileged functions on build servers, HSMs, and FL-1 and TX-1 MES servers are logged and sent to the SIEM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: SSO locks accounts after 10 failed attempts in 15 minutes; MES stations at FL-1 and TX-1 inherit SSO policy.
Engineering workstations lock after 15 minutes. Plant stations lock after 30 minutes of inactivity with badge-tap unlock at FL-1 and TX-1.
Remote administration uses the zero-trust access service and PAM. Gap: two station vendors reach MN-1 programming stations with their own remote tools outside PAM (POAM-007).
evidence: Remote access inventory; P07 AC-17 results

implementation_statement: Plant wireless is limited to handheld scanners on a separate SSID with certificate authentication; programming stations are wired only.
Security awareness and training policy (POL-05) and STD-05.1 apply to all DSF-MES users.
Annual awareness training and monthly phishing simulations for all workforce, including plant operators with system access.

Role-based training: secure coding for developers, signing custodian training, and OT security training for plant engineers. Gap: 18% of device software engineers are overdue for the annual secure coding module (POAM-016).
Audit logging standard STD-01.4 (P06) applies.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Logged events include repository pushes and merges, branch protection changes, pipeline runs, signing requests and approvals, HSM key use, artifact promotions, MES recipe and firmware image changes, and privileged sessions.
evidence: STD-01.4 event list; SIEM source list

implementation_statement: Audit records include time, source, user or service identity, event type, object, and outcome.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: SOC reviews signing, artifact promotion, and privileged events daily through SIEM use cases. Gap: the legacy IV-300 signing workstation and the MN-1 MES server do not send logs to the SIEM; their logs are reviewed by hand monthly (POAM-011).
evidence: SOC review records; SIEM source list

implementation_statement: SIEM correlates signing, repository, and identity events with automated alerts (for example, a signing request outside a release window).
Repository, build, signing, and identity logs are correlated in the SIEM to reconstruct a release end to end.
Logs are forwarded to the write-once log archive account; SOC staff cannot delete archived logs.
Build and signing logs are retained 1 year online and for the life of the device plus 2 years in the archive, to support design history and 806.20 record needs.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Audit generation is enabled on the repository tenant, build orchestrator, signing portal, HSMs, artifact repository, and FL-1 and TX-1 MES.
Assessment, authorization, and monitoring standard STD-01.2 applies.
Internal Audit assesses DSF-MES annually using SP 800-53A procedures (P07).
Assessors are Internal Audit staff independent of engineering, manufacturing, and security operations.
evidence: Internal Audit charter; P07 independence statement

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Interconnection agreements cover the DDC update service, eQMS, ERP, the source repository SaaS, the PLM SaaS, and CMO-1 and CMO-2 image deliveries.
Weaknesses are tracked in the enterprise POA&M in the GRC platform (P07 poam.csv).
The COO grants the internal authorization decision on the CISO's recommendation (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring: monthly metrics on signing events, build pipeline integrity checks, vulnerability SLAs, and plant OT findings reported to the CISO and the system owner.
Configuration and change management standard STD-01.5 and procedure PRC-01.3 apply.
Baselines are defined as code for build nodes and FL-1 and TX-1 MES servers and stations. Gap: MN-1 servers and stations have no documented baseline (POAM-009).

control_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency
responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Configuration management tooling reapplies baselines to build nodes daily and reports drift.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Firmware and cloud releases follow design change control in PLM: change request, impact analysis, verification, and release approval before the artifact is promoted and signed. Gap: 3 of 40 sampled firmware releases were promoted to the update service before the PLM release record was approved (POAM-010).
evidence: PLM release records; artifact promotion logs; P07 CM-3 results

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Pipeline changes and MES recipe changes are tested in staging environments before production.
Security impact analysis is part of every design change record, including whether the change affects cybersecurity content of a marketing submission.
evidence: Change records with security impact field

implementation_statement: Changes to pipeline definitions, signing policies, and FL-1 and TX-1 MES require PAM sessions and approved change tickets. Gap: MN-1 station operators have local administrator rights (POAM-009).
evidence: PAM session records; MN-1 local admin export

implementation_statement: Hardened settings follow the build node and OT station benchmarks in STD-01.5. Gap: MN-1 stations deviate from 14 of 40 checked settings (POAM-009).
Build nodes run only pipeline services; FL-1 and TX-1 stations block USB storage and non-allowlisted software. Gap: MN-1 stations allow USB storage (POAM-009).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Build nodes and FL-1 and TX-1 stations use application allowlisting (allow by exception).

Inventory covers build nodes, HSMs, signing keys, MES servers, and stations; the SBOM service keeps a component inventory for every released image. Gap: OT asset inventory is 88% complete at MN-1, and SBOMs exist for about 40% of third-party firmware modules (POAM-005).
Inventory is updated automatically on install, removal, and update through agents and passive OT discovery at FL-1 and TX-1.
Contingency and disaster recovery standard STD-03.3 applies.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The DSF-MES contingency plan covers the signing service, build farm, artifact repository, manufacturing PKI, and MES, with RTOs from P05 (BP-04 RTO 24 h; BP-07 to BP-09 RTO 48 h).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The plan is coordinated with the DDC contingency plan (update service) and plant emergency plans.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Annual recovery test of the build farm and artifact repository. Gap: secondary HSM failover has not been tested since 2025-06 (POAM-012).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Artifact repository, HSM cluster, and source mirror are replicated to DC-2, about 1,000 miles from DC-1.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: DC-2 is the alternate processing site for signing and artifact services; plants can run from cached released images.
Dual carriers at DC-1, DC-2, and each plant with cellular failover.
Artifact repository, build metadata, PLM exports, and FL-1 and TX-1 MES configurations are backed up nightly to immutable storage. Gap: MN-1 MES backups have never been restore-tested (POAM-009).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Restores are tested quarterly for the artifact repository and MES configurations at FL-1 and TX-1.
Backups are encrypted with keys in the enterprise key management service.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Recovery procedures rebuild build nodes from infrastructure code. Gap: the 2026-05 test took 30 hours against the 24-hour RTO (POAM-012).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Transaction recovery for the artifact repository database uses point-in-time recovery.
Identification and authentication standard STD-02.2 applies.
Engineers and release staff authenticate through SSO with MFA. Gap: MN-1 MES and stations use shared operator logins on a legacy directory (POAM-007).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged access to build, signing, HSM, and MES servers requires phishing-resistant MFA.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Non-privileged access to the repository, PLM, and signing portal requires MFA.
Programming stations at FL-1 and TX-1 authenticate to the plant image cache and the manufacturing PKI with device certificates.
Authenticator management follows STD-02.2. Gap: default vendor passwords were found on 6 MN-1 programming fixture controllers during P07 testing on 2026-08-11 (POAM-008).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Passwords meet STD-02.2 (14 characters minimum, breached-password screening).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The manufacturing PKI and signing service validate certificate paths and revocation status; private keys for signing and issuing CAs are non-exportable in HSMs.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Contract manufacturer and supplier users are federated through the identity platform with sponsor approval and MFA.
Incident response policy POL-03 applies.
Incident response training for SOC, PSIRT, and release engineering on-call staff.
Annual tabletop exercises; the 2026 exercise included a signing key compromise scenario.
Incidents affecting the build or signing path follow PRC-03.1 and the P08 runbook, including stopping releases, revoking keys, and rebuilding from known-good sources.
Incidents are tracked in SOC case management.
Workforce reports incidents within 1 hour; PSIRT and the CQRO decide FDA reporting (P08).
The enterprise incident response plan includes product security and SEC materiality procedures (PRC-03.2).
Maintenance standard STD-01.6 applies.
Station and MES maintenance is scheduled through plant maintenance systems with records.
Nonlocal maintenance of build and FL-1 and TX-1 MES servers goes through PAM with session recording.
Retired build nodes, HSMs, and station drives are sanitized or destroyed with certificates; HSMs are zeroized under dual control.
Access to DC-1 and DC-2 cages and plant server rooms is authorized by list and reviewed quarterly.
Badge-controlled data center cages and plant server rooms; HSMs in locked racks with two-person access.
Planning policy is part of POL-01 and the policy hierarchy.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: This SSP is maintained and reviewed annually and after major changes.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) are acknowledged annually.
Personnel security procedures apply.
Background screening for all workforce; enhanced screening for signing custodians and HSM administrators.
Terminations trigger same-day disablement through identity governance. Gap: MN-1 legacy directory disablement is manual; 2 of 25 sampled MN-1 terminations were disabled 2 and 5 days late (POAM-017).
Sanctions under PRC-01.1.
Risk assessment standard STD-01.1 applies.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: DSF-MES categorized under FIPS 199 as a model (section 6).
Annual enterprise risk analysis (P01) plus product threat models that include the build and update path as related systems.
Supply chain risk assessment covers source repository, build tools, HSM vendor, station vendors, and contract manufacturers.

Authenticated scanning of build and MES servers monthly; container and dependency scanning in every pipeline. Gap: authenticated scan coverage is 82% of build infrastructure; MN-1 OT has passive discovery only (POAM-020).
Published CVD policy with a 3-business-day acknowledgment commitment covers vulnerabilities in firmware, the build pipeline, and the update path.
Risk responses are recorded in the risk register and POA&M.
Criticality analysis identifies signing keys, the manufacturing PKI, and release promotion as critical functions.
The product development life cycle under the QMS includes security activities at each phase (threat modeling, security requirements, testing, SBOM).
Acquisition contracts for build tools, HSMs, stations, and firmware modules include security requirements and SBOM delivery terms (new contracts since 2025).
Secure design principles in STD-01.8 (secure product development) apply to device and pipeline design.
External services (source repository SaaS, PLM SaaS, cloud runners, HSM vendor support) are assessed and monitored. Gap: CMO-2's security assessment is 7 months overdue (POAM-013).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Developer configuration management: all firmware and pipeline code in version control with protected branches; changes traceable to PLM change records.
Static analysis, software composition analysis, fuzzing for device interfaces, and independent penetration testing before major releases.
evidence: Test reports in the design history file

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Development process and tools are defined and controlled. Gap: signed build provenance is produced only for cloud software, not firmware (POAM-004).
Unsupported components are tracked with replacement plans. Gap: MN-1 MES servers run an unsupported operating system (POAM-009).
System and communications protection is covered by POL-04 and STD-04.1.
Build, signing, and PKI zones are segmented at DC-1 and DC-2; FL-1 and TX-1 OT networks are segmented by zone with conduits to MES. Gap: MN-1 OT is flat with its office network (POAM-006).

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default, allow by exception, on build, signing, and plant OT firewalls.
TLS 1.2 or higher between repository, build, signing, artifact, and plant image cache services. Gap: MN-1 MES to station traffic uses an unencrypted legacy protocol (POAM-018).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Signing and PKI keys are generated and held in FIPS 140-validated HSMs under key ceremonies with 3 custodians. Gap: IV-300 1.x keys live on a standalone workstation outside the HSM service (POAM-001).
FIPS-validated cryptography for signing, TLS, and storage encryption.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The manufacturing PKI issues device identity certificates under a documented certificate policy.
Artifact repository, build metadata, and backups are encrypted at rest.
Encryption at rest uses keys in the enterprise key management service.
System and information integrity is covered by POL-01 and STD-01.5.
Build nodes are patched within 14 days (critical 72 hours). Gap: MN-1 servers and stations are not patched to SLA (POAM-009).
EDR on build nodes and engineering workstations; OT-safe malware scanning on FL-1 and TX-1 stations.
SOC monitors build, signing, and identity events 24x7; passive OT monitoring at FL-1 and TX-1. Gap: no OT monitoring at MN-1 (POAM-006).
PSIRT receives ISAO, CISA, and supplier advisories and matches them to SBOMs.

Firmware images are signed and verified at every programming station at FL-1 and TX-1 and by devices at boot and before update. Gap: MN-1 IV-300 stations verify images with a checksum only (POAM-019).
evidence: Station verification logs; P07 SI-7 results

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The artifact repository re-verifies signatures and hashes of released images daily.
Integrity failures create SOC cases automatically.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Pipeline and signing portal inputs are validated (artifact type, product line, version, and approver checks).
Release, signing, and production records are retained per the QMS record retention schedule.
Supply chain risk management plan covers software suppliers, firmware modules, and contract manufacturers.
Supply chain controls require SBOMs from firmware module suppliers for new contracts. Gap: SBOMs received for about 40% of existing third-party firmware modules (POAM-005).
Acquisition strategies favor authorized distributors and qualified suppliers.
Supplier security assessments on a risk-based cycle. Gap: CMO-2 assessment overdue (POAM-013).
Incoming inspection of programmed subassemblies from CMO-1 includes firmware version and signature checks.
Component authenticity: CMO-1 subassemblies carry device certificates from the manufacturing PKI. Gap: CMO-2 programs HB-40 boards outside the PKI (POAM-013).
evidence: PKI issuance logs; CMO-2 process review

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Planned: signing and release logs will be hash-chained and signed before archiving (2027-03-31).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Non-repudiation: the signing portal binds each signing to two named approvers with MFA and records them in the HSM audit log. Gap: legacy IV-300 signing approvals are by email (POAM-001).

control_name: Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes
responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: The pipeline blocks promotion of an artifact without a linked approved change record for current product lines; exceptions route to release engineering management.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Separate test environments for pipeline changes and MES recipe changes.

control_name: Automated Access Enforcement and Audit Records
responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Access enforcement for pipeline and signing policy changes is automated through PAM and code review, with audit records.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Signing keys are available from the secondary HSM cluster at DC-2 using key backup shares held by 3 custodians.

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Integrity violations (signature mismatch at a station or in the repository) notify release engineering and the SOC automatically.
Planned: stations will quarantine a lot automatically on an integrity failure (FL-1 and TX-1 by 2027-03-31; MN-1 with POAM-019).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Code authentication: devices and stations verify the vendor signature before installing firmware (current product lines).
Signed components: stations at FL-1 and TX-1 refuse unsigned images. Gap: MN-1 stations and CMO-2 do not (POAM-019, POAM-013).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Planned: reproducible firmware builds with independent rebuild verification before signing (2027-06-30).

responsible_role: Director of Build and Release Engineering
implementation_statement: Planned: signed provenance attestations for every firmware build, linked to the SBOM (POAM-004, 2027-03-31).
